reason: The hypothesis synthesizes separate findings on lattice-distortion-enhanced creep resistance (P3, P7) and edge-dislocation-controlled strength (P11, P24) with the observation of edge dislocation dominance in a different HEA (P19) to propose a new mechanism for toughness in WTaTiVZr, a material whose tensile toughness has not been studied. It links these ideas through crack-tip blunting, which none of the passages explicitly connects to lattice distortion in this alloy, and applies them to a controlled comparison with pure tungsten that resolves the gap in toughness data.
copied_elements: severe lattice distortion alters dislocation behavior (P3, P7)
edge dislocations control strength in refractory HEAs (P11, P24)
edge dislocation dominance in BCC HEAs (P19, P20, P21)
high-temperature inert-environment fracture toughness testing of tungsten (P6, P8, P30)
